I could not verify this from first principles, and I don't have a reliable derivation of the count. My best recollection is that the lattice of quasivarieties of Sugihara algebras has continuum cardinality, and that only finitely many of its members have the amalgamation property. I believe the count is 4, but treat that as a recollection, not a checked result. Confirming it would require the specific literature on quasivarieties of Sugihara algebras.

ANSWER: 4
